Identify correct reactivity order for $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction

(i), (ii), (iii) as shown in the figure.
solution:
Carbocations formed (as shown in the figure): from (i) aromatic, but O exerts maximum $-I$ effect; from (ii) aromatic, N exerts less $-I$; from (iii) anti-aromatic (least stable).

Hence reactivity: (ii) > (i) > (iii).

stem: Which of the following can be used to prevent the decomposition of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$?
solution: Urea acts as a stabilising agent. It prevents the decomposition of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$.

stem: Primary amines can be distinguished from secondary and tertiary amines by reacting with
solution: $1^\circ$ amines (aliphatic and aromatic) react with $\text{CHCl}_3/\text{KOH}$ to yield isocyanide (foul smelling). This is the carbylamine test, which is not given by $2^\circ$ and $3^\circ$ amines.

stem: Which of the following is a hypnotic drug?
solution: Hypnotic drugs induce sleep and are habit forming; common examples are luminal and seconal.

stem: Which one of the following exhibits geometrical isomerism?
solution: Alkenes having two different groups on each end of the double bond show geometrical isomerism ($\text{Ca}_2\text{b}_2$-type excluded; $\text{abC=Cab}$, $\text{abC=Ccd}$ types show it). 1,2-Dibromopropene and 2,3-dibromobut-2-ene qualify; 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene does not.
Mg burns in $\text{CO}_2$ to give MgO and C: $2\text{Mg} + \text{CO}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MgO} + \text{C}$.

stem: Which of the following catalyst is used in preparation of high density polythene?
solution: High density polythene is formed when addition polymerisation of ethene takes place in a hydrocarbon solvent in presence of a catalyst such as Ziegler–Natta catalyst.

stem: Which of the following acts as the stationary phase in paper chromatography?
solution: Chromatography paper contains water trapped in it, which acts as the stationary phase.

options: The colloidal solution of a liquid in liquid is called gel
Hardy Schulze rule is related with coagulation
Brownian movement and Tyndall effect are shown by colloidal system
Gold number is a measure of the protective power of lyophilic colloid
solution: A colloid of liquid in liquid is called an emulsion. A colloid of liquid in solid is a gel.
